paper_title: Prediction of plasma ctDNA fraction and prognostic implications of liquid biopsy in advanced prostate cancer
prediction_task: ctDNA fraction prediction from clinical parameters + prognostic implications in metastatic prostate cancer

reviewer_concerns.concern_text: Most samples were already analyzed in previous publications from same group. Prognostic association of ctDNA is not novel — the strength is the AI prediction tool. Title and narrative should center on the predictive tool, not the prognostic role of ctDNA.
reviewer_concerns.author_response: Restructured narrative to emphasize the prediction tool as main contribution.

reviewer_concerns.concern_text: Patients exposed to taxanes had increased cfDNA and ctDNA fraction. How does the prediction model account for ctDNA variance due to different therapies if these variables were not incorporated?
reviewer_concerns.author_response: Added therapy-stratified analysis and discussed model behavior across treatment lines.

reviewer_concerns.concern_text: cfDNA concentration seems to be the highest predictor of ctDNA fraction and is inter-correlated with LDH/ALP. But authors don't explore cfDNA concentration's prognostic role or compare it to ctDNA.
reviewer_concerns.author_response: Added cfDNA concentration as standalone prognostic factor comparison.

reviewer_strengths.text: Elegant approach with uniform harmonized analysis pipeline. Large cohort gives strength. The AI prediction tool is a powerful contribution for biomarker studies and patient stratification.
